subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should local avatar failures keep generic direct-route 404s with clearer UI diagnostics, or should `/avatar/{agentId}` expose specific statuses for oversized, missing, or rejected files?
rationale: The remaining behavior sits on an authenticated workspace file-serving route, where more helpful errors improve UX but can reveal local file or policy details if exposed at the endpoint boundary.

options.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep direct image fetches generic and use the existing `avatarReason` metadata plus Quick Settings/chat surfaces to explain oversized or missing avatars.

options.title: Expose Endpoint Errors
options.body: Return specific statuses such as 413 or 400 from the direct avatar route after security review proves no sensitive path details leak.

options.title: Fold Into Remote Avatar Contract
options.body: Defer this local diagnostics choice into the broader Control UI avatar contract tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41201.

recommendation.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
recommendation.body: Keep direct image fetches generic and use the existing `avatarReason` metadata plus Quick Settings/chat surfaces to explain oversized or missing avatars.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle owns the strongest history signal for both the avatar feature and the later local file-serving hardening.
